item.content:encoded:
The ITU-UNDP Responsible Digital Transformation: Impact Assessments for AI and Data Governance course is a free, four-week professional training opportunity designed to help policymakers and practitioners understand how to assess the human rights, social, and governance implications of artificial intelligence, digital public infrastructure, and data-driven public services.

As governments around the world accelerate digital transformation, artificial intelligence and data-driven technologies are increasingly being integrated into public-sector systems. These technologies can improve the efficiency, accessibility, and quality of public services, but they can also create significant risks relating to fairness, transparency, accountability, discrimination, privacy, and inclusion.

This online course, coordinated by the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), is designed to move participants beyond high-level discussions about responsible technology and equip them with practical tools that can be applied to real governance decisions.

The training will guide participants through a structured impact-assessment process based on UNDP’s Human Rights Impact Assessment (HRIA) methodology. By the end of the course, participants are expected to develop a draft impact assessment and mitigation plan for a real-world digital or AI governance use case relevant to their own institutional context.

The course is offered with generous support from the Global Gateway strategy of the European Union, making it free for selected participants.

ITU-UNDP Responsible Digital Transformation Course 2026: At a Glance

  • Course title: Responsible Digital Transformation: Impact Assessments for AI and Data Governance
  • Organisers: International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)
  • Course level: Intermediate
  • Format: Online training
  • Duration: 4 weeks
  • Training dates: 6 October 2026 to 27 October 2026
  • Application period: 11 August 2026 to 19 September 2026
  • Application deadline: 19 September 2026
  • Language: English
  • Training topic: Digital transformation
  • Cost: $0 for selected participants
  • Course coordinators: Angel Draev and Queenie Tam
  • Course contact: queenie.tam@undp.org
  • Target audience: Policymakers and practitioners working in areas related to digital transformation, AI governance, data governance, and public services

What Is the Responsible Digital Transformation Course?

The Responsible Digital Transformation course is a professional learning programme focused on the practical governance of artificial intelligence and data-driven technologies.

Public institutions are increasingly using digital technologies to provide services, process information, make decisions, and interact with citizens. While these systems can offer considerable benefits, they may also introduce risks that governments and practitioners need to identify and manage.

For example, an AI or data-driven public-service system could raise questions about:

  • Whether different groups are treated fairly.
  • Whether decisions are transparent and explainable.
  • Whether people can challenge automated decisions.
  • Whether personal data is adequately protected.
  • Whether particular communities could experience unintended harm.
  • Whether digital services are accessible to everyone.
  • Whether technological systems reinforce existing inequalities.
  • Whether institutions have suitable governance and accountability mechanisms.

The course is intended to help participants systematically examine these issues rather than approaching responsible digital transformation only as a matter of broad ethical principles.

Participants will learn how to assess a specific technology or use case, identify potential impacts and risks, and formulate mitigation and governance recommendations.

Why This Course Is Important in 2026

Digital transformation is rapidly changing how governments operate.

Artificial intelligence is increasingly being explored or deployed in areas such as the following:

  • Public administration
  • Healthcare
  • Education
  • Social protection
  • Public finance
  • Citizen services
  • Identity systems
  • Data management
  • Decision-making
  • Public information services
  • Digital public infrastructure

The expansion of these technologies means that policymakers and practitioners need more than technical knowledge. They also need to understand the social, legal, human rights, and governance implications of digital systems.

Responsible digital transformation seeks to ensure that technological innovation does not come at the expense of fundamental rights, fairness, inclusion, and accountability.

This makes practical impact-assessment expertise increasingly relevant for governments, international organisations, development institutions, regulators, public-sector professionals, and other stakeholders working with emerging digital technologies.

What Participants Will Learn

A central objective of the programme is to help participants apply practical impact-assessment tools to real governance decisions.

The course builds on the UNDP Human Rights Impact Assessment methodology and guides participants through a structured process for examining the potential consequences of digital and AI-related interventions.

By the end of the course, participants are expected to have developed a draft impact assessment and mitigation plan based on a real-world digital or AI governance use case relevant to their institutional context.

This makes the programme strongly practice-oriented.

Rather than simply learning concepts, participants will be expected to apply what they learn to a specific scenario.

Core Learning Areas

Although the course focuses broadly on responsible digital transformation, several major themes are central to the learning experience.

1. Artificial Intelligence Governance

Participants will examine governance questions associated with AI systems used in public-sector environments.

This includes understanding how AI can affect decision-making and public services and identifying governance mechanisms that can help institutions manage associated risks.

2. Data Governance

Data is a fundamental component of many modern digital systems.

Effective data governance involves considering how data is collected, managed, processed, used and protected, as well as how these processes can affect individuals and communities.

Participants will learn how data-related considerations fit into broader impact assessments.

3. Digital Public Infrastructure

Digital public infrastructure can provide the foundation for large-scale public services and digital interactions.

However, the design and implementation of digital infrastructure can also create important questions around inclusion, access, governance, and rights.

Participants will examine these issues as part of the wider digital-governance perspective.

4. Human Rights Impact Assessment

The programme draws upon UNDP’s Human Rights Impact Assessment methodology.

The approach provides a structured way of examining how a proposed digital or technological intervention may affect people’s rights and identifying measures that can reduce potential harm.

This is particularly important when technologies are deployed at scale or used in high-impact public-service environments.

5. Risk Identification

Participants will learn to identify potential risks associated with a particular digital or AI use case.

This includes considering not only intended outcomes but also possible unintended consequences.

6. Impact Assessment

A major component of the programme is assessing how a proposed technology, system, or intervention may affect different stakeholders.

This encourages participants to move from general discussions about responsible technology to structured analysis.

7. Mitigation Planning

Identifying risks is only one part of responsible governance.

Participants will also develop mitigation and governance recommendations designed to address identified risks and reduce potential negative impacts.

Practical Outcome of the Course

One of the strongest features of this training is its practical final output.

By completing the programme, participants are expected to develop a draft impact assessment and mitigation plan for a real-world digital or AI governance use case.

The use case should be relevant to the participant’s institutional context.

This could make the learning experience particularly valuable for professionals who are already working on digital transformation initiatives, technology policy, public-sector innovation, or related areas.

The project-based nature of the course may also help participants translate the concepts covered during the training into a practical framework that can inform their professional work.

Who Should Apply?

The course is particularly relevant to policymakers and practitioners involved in digital transformation and technology governance.

Professionals who may find the programme especially useful include those working in or around:

  • Government ministries and departments
  • Public-sector digital transformation
  • Digital policy
  • AI governance
  • Data governance
  • Technology policy
  • Digital public infrastructure
  • Public-service delivery
  • Information and communications technology
  • Regulation
  • Human rights
  • Public administration
  • Development policy
  • International development
  • Digital inclusion
  • Responsible innovation

Because the course is designed at an intermediate level, it may be especially suitable for professionals who already have some exposure to digital transformation, public-sector technology, governance or related areas and want to develop more practical impact-assessment capabilities.

Is There a Specific Academic Degree Requirement?

The information provided does not specify a mandatory academic degree or particular university qualification.

Instead, the course is framed around professional relevance, particularly for policymakers and practitioners.

Applicants should therefore focus on demonstrating how their professional responsibilities, institutional role, or experience relates to digital transformation, AI, data governance, digital public services, or related areas.

Is the Course Open to People From All Countries?

The programme’s registration information states that, unless otherwise specified, ITU Academy training courses are open to all interested professionals irrespective of race, ethnicity, age, gender, religion, economic status, and other diverse backgrounds.

The organisers also state that they strongly encourage registrations from female participants and participants from developing countries.

The programme specifically notes that this includes

  • Least developed countries
  • Small island developing states
  • Landlocked developing countries

Therefore, the stated eligibility approach is broad and inclusive rather than being restricted to one race, ethnic group, or geographical region.

Race, Gender, and Diversity Eligibility

The course does not identify a racial or ethnic restriction.

The registration information expressly states that ITU Academy courses are generally open to interested professionals regardless of

  • Race
  • Ethnicity
  • Age
  • Gender
  • Religion
  • Economic status
  • Other diverse backgrounds

The organisers also encourage greater participation by women and people from developing countries.

This means that the programme is designed to promote broad and diverse participation in digital governance capacity development.

Is This Course Free?

Yes.

The course is listed at a price of $0, and the programme description states that it is free for selected participants.

The opportunity is supported by the Global Gateway strategy of the European Union.

Applicants should distinguish between being able to apply and being selected for the programme. The course description specifically states that it is free for selected participants.

Course Duration and Training Dates

The programme lasts for four weeks.

Training period

6 October 2026 to 27 October 2026

This means selected participants should be available to engage throughout the four-week learning period.

Because the programme involves structured learning and the development of a practical impact assessment, applicants should consider their professional workload and availability before registering.

Application Period and Deadline

Applications are open from:

11 August 2026

and close on:

19 September 2026

Application deadline: 19 September 2026

Interested professionals should ensure that their applications are submitted before the stated deadline.

It is advisable to apply well before the closing date rather than waiting until the final day, particularly when the application may require applicants to provide information about their professional background, institutional context, or relevant experience.

APPLY HERE

Course Language

The training is delivered in English.

Applicants should therefore be comfortable participating in an English-language professional learning environment.

This may include understanding course materials, participating in learning activities and completing assignments or practical work in English.

Course Level

The course is classified as Intermediate.

This is significant for prospective participants because the programme is not presented as a basic introductory course to digital technology.

Participants who already have some familiarity with digital transformation, public-sector innovation, AI, data governance, or related policy questions may be particularly well positioned to benefit from the training.

The Role of AI and Data in Public Services

One of the central premises of the course is that AI and data-driven systems are increasingly influencing public-service delivery.

Governments may use these technologies to improve efficiency and support decision-making, but their deployment can also have far-reaching implications.

For example, an automated system used in a public institution may influence who receives a service, how resources are allocated, or how information is processed.

This creates an important governance question: How can institutions adopt digital technologies while ensuring that the systems remain fair, transparent, accountable, and inclusive?

The course is intended to help participants approach precisely these kinds of questions using a structured impact-assessment framework.

From Principles to Practical Governance

Many discussions about responsible AI focus on broad principles such as fairness, transparency, and accountability.

While these principles are important, applying them to a real project can be considerably more complex.

A public institution may need to determine the following:

  1. What exactly is the technology being used for?
  2. Who could be affected by the system?
  3. What potential risks could emerge?
  4. Which rights or interests might be affected?
  5. What evidence is available?
  6. What safeguards should be introduced?
  7. Who should be responsible for monitoring the system?
  8. How should risks be mitigated?
  9. How can the institution demonstrate accountability?

The ITU-UNDP course seeks to give participants a structured approach to tackling these practical questions.

Why Human Rights Matter in AI Governance

Artificial intelligence and data systems can have consequences for people’s everyday lives.

When technologies are used in public-sector environments, the consequences can become particularly significant because public institutions often make decisions that directly affect citizens and communities.

A human-rights-based impact assessment can help institutions identify potential negative consequences before or during implementation and consider appropriate safeguards.

This makes human rights impact assessment an important complement to technical and operational assessments of digital technologies.

Benefits of Taking the ITU-UNDP Course

Professional capacity building

Participants can strengthen their practical understanding of impact assessment for AI, digital, and data-driven governance.

Application to real-world work

The course requires participants to develop a draft assessment and mitigation plan linked to a real-world use case.

Exposure to an international learning environment

The programme is delivered through an international institutional partnership involving ITU and UNDP.

Strong relevance to emerging policy challenges

AI governance, data governance, and responsible digital transformation are becoming increasingly important areas of public policy and institutional decision-making.

Practical risk-management skills

Participants can improve their ability to identify risks, analyse impacts, and formulate mitigation recommendations.

Human rights perspective

The programme introduces an approach rooted in UNDP’s Human Rights Impact Assessment methodology.

Professional development

The knowledge gained can potentially support professionals involved in policymaking, governance, regulation, digital transformation, and public service innovation.

Inclusive participation

The course is designed to welcome professionals across diverse racial, ethnic, gender, religious, and socioeconomic backgrounds.

How to Make Your Application Stronger

Although applicants should always follow the official registration instructions, prospective participants can strengthen their preparation by clearly connecting their professional experience to the themes of the course.

Demonstrate your relevance

Explain how your current role or professional responsibilities connect with digital transformation, AI, data, public services, governance, technology, or policy.

Identify a relevant use case

Because the course culminates in a draft impact assessment and mitigation plan for a real-world use case, applicants should consider whether there is a digital or AI-related issue within their institutional environment that could benefit from this type of analysis.

Highlight your motivation

Explain why responsible digital transformation matters to your work and why you want to develop practical impact-assessment skills.

Connect the training to institutional needs

A strong application can demonstrate how the skills gained from the course could contribute to improved decision-making, governance, digital service delivery, or risk management within the applicant’s professional environment.

Show readiness for intermediate-level learning

Applicants should demonstrate sufficient familiarity with their professional field to engage meaningfully with governance, risk, and impact-assessment concepts.

Who Is Most Likely to Benefit From This Opportunity?

This training can be particularly valuable for professionals who are already involved in digital transformation and want to deepen their understanding of responsible governance.

It may be especially relevant to:

  • Government officials involved in digital transformation programmes.
  • Policymakers developing digital or AI-related policies.
  • Professionals working on data governance.
  • Public-sector technology specialists.
  • Digital transformation practitioners.
  • AI governance professionals.
  • Regulators and policy advisers.
  • Development practitioners working on digital transformation.
  • Professionals involved in digital public infrastructure.
  • Public-service innovation teams.
  • Human rights and governance practitioners.
  • Professionals responsible for technology-related risk and accountability.

Visit HERE for more information about the ITU-UNDP Free Online Course 2026.

ITU and UNDP Partnership

The course brings together the expertise and institutional perspectives of two major international organisations.

The International Telecommunication Union is the United Nations specialised agency for information and communication technologies, while the United Nations Development Programme works across countries to support development, governance, and sustainable development priorities.

The collaboration creates a learning environment that connects digital technology with development, governance, and human rights considerations.

The programme is also supported through the European Union’s Global Gateway strategy, which provides support for initiatives connected to sustainable connectivity, digital transformation, and related development priorities.

Important Information for Applicants

Before applying, prospective participants should carefully consider the following:

  • The application period runs from 11 August to 19 September 2026.
  • The final application deadline is 19 September 2026.
  • The course runs from 6 October to 27 October 2026.
  • The programme lasts four weeks.
  • The course is delivered in English.
  • The course is classified as Intermediate.
  • The listed price is $0 for selected participants.
  • The programme focuses on AI, data governance, digital public infrastructure, and digital public services.
  • The training is based on UNDP’s Human Rights Impact Assessment methodology.
  • Participants are expected to produce a draft impact assessment and mitigation plan for a relevant real-world use case.
  • The course is particularly relevant to policymakers and practitioners.
  • ITU Academy’s stated inclusion policy means applicants are generally welcomed regardless of race, ethnicity, age, gender, religion, or economic status.
  • Women and participants from developing countries are strongly encouraged to register.
  • Developing-country participation explicitly includes least developed countries, small island developing states, and landlocked developing countries.

How to Apply

Interested professionals should proceed through the ITU Academy registration process for the Responsible Digital Transformation: Impact Assessments for AI and Data Governance course.

Application period: 11 August 2026 – 19 September 2026

Deadline: 19 September 2026

Applicants should review the official registration information carefully and ensure they satisfy any detailed participation requirements associated with the course before submitting their application.

Conclusion

The ITU-UNDP Responsible Digital Transformation: Impact Assessments for AI and Data Governance course represents a timely professional development opportunity for policymakers and practitioners navigating the increasingly complex relationship between technology, government, and society.

As artificial intelligence, digital public infrastructure, and data-driven systems become more deeply integrated into public services, institutions need professionals who can identify risks, assess impacts, and develop practical governance measures that promote fairness, transparency, accountability, and inclusion.

This four-week intermediate course provides participants with an opportunity to develop precisely those capabilities. By building on UNDP’s Human Rights Impact Assessment methodology and requiring participants to develop a draft impact assessment and mitigation plan for a real-world use case, the programme goes beyond theoretical discussion and emphasises practical application.

The opportunity is particularly relevant for professionals working in digital transformation, AI governance, data governance, public administration, technology policy, digital public infrastructure, and related development fields. It also has a broad inclusion approach, welcoming interested professionals regardless of race, ethnicity, age, gender, religion, and economic status, while strongly encouraging participation from women and professionals from developing countries.

With applications open from 11 August 2026 until 19 September 2026, professionals interested in responsible AI, digital governance, and human-centred digital transformation should consider applying before the deadline.

Application Deadline: 19 September 2026

Training Dates: 6 October 2026 – 27 October 2026

Official Course: ITU Academy – Responsible Digital Transformation: Impact Assessments for AI and Data Governance.

item.content:encoded:
Key Details

  • Opportunity: Code for Good Hackathon / 2027 Software Engineer Program Summer Internship
  • Host: JPMorganChase Tech for Social Good
  • Location: United States — Chicago, Columbus, Houston, Jersey City, New York, Palo Alto, Plano, Tampa and Wilmington
  • Program: Full-time Summer Internship
  • Expected Graduation: December 2027–June 2028
  • Eligible Fields: Computer Science, Information Science, Information Technology, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Big Data and related fields
  • Work Authorization: Applicants must be authorized to work in the U.S.; JPMorganChase does not provide employment-based immigration sponsorship for this program.
  • Code for Good Events:
    • Brooklyn, NY: October 16–17, 2026 — deadline September 18, 2026
    • Columbus, OH: November 6–7, 2026 — deadline October 9, 2026
  • Overall Job Posting Deadline: November 6, 2026, 5:00 AM
  • Salary: Approximately $45.67–$60.10/hour, depending on location
  • Potential Outcome: Participation in Code for Good may lead to consideration for the 2027 Software Engineer Program Summer Internship.
  • Application: Applicants submit a resume and complete the required application process, including a HackerRank coding challenge if selected for the next stage.

Job Description

Join Code for Good, a social impact hackathon hosted by JPMorganChase’s Tech for Social Good team, where your coding skills can make a difference for nonprofit organizations. Discover if a career in financial services technology is your calling, as you unlock your potential with a dynamic team of innovative technologists. Participating in Code for Good may also lead to an opportunity for you to learn more about and be considered for a 2027 Software Engineer Program Summer Internship.

ABOUT THE PROGRAM/EVENT

Tech for Social Good at JPMorganChase is focused on driving impact in our communities through the skills of our tech workforce. By attending Code for Good, you will collaborate with our expert technologists to creatively address real-world technology challenges faced by nonprofit organizations, fostering innovation and impact. This experience offers you the chance to network with fellow aspiring software engineers across the country and engage with our recruiting teams, providing insight into the software engineering role at JPMorganChase. Over two days (Friday – Saturday), you and your team will develop a tech solution for a leading nonprofit, with travel expenses covered under certain conditions. Your participation in the Code for Good hackathon may also lead to an opportunity for you to learn more about and be considered for a 2027 Software Engineer Program Summer Internship.

As an Early Careers Software Engineer Intern in our Software Engineer Program, you will play a vital role in building and optimizing digital applications and systems that serve millions globally. You will start with an induction that introduces our technology strategies, products, and systems, and provides an overview of our technology community. Working in a collaborative team, you will partner with peers and experienced software engineers to enhance your skills, share ideas and feedback, and help deliver reliable solutions in a modern engineering environment. This internship offers a chance to gain deeper insights into our work culture through networking events, senior speaker sessions, and peer-mentorship programs.

At the end of the summer, top performers may be invited to join us for a full-time role upon graduation. We will be filling our classes on a rolling basis, so we strongly encourage you to submit your application as early as possible before job postings close.

APPLY NOW

Job Responsibilities

  • Develop skills through ongoing training, mentorship, and access to senior leaders.
  • Design, develop, test, and troubleshoot software solutions.
  • Write secure, high-quality code in at least one programming language, following established standards and best practices.
  • Collaborate with engineers, managers, and stakeholders across teams to understand problems, share ideas and feedback, and deliver reliable solutions.
  • Communicate clearly in writing and verbally by articulating problems, documenting solutions, and effectively prompting approved AI-assisted development tools to produce high-quality outputs.
  • Leverage approved AI development tools (for example, code generation, refactoring, testcreation, and documentation) to improve code quality and productivity, while validating outputs through peer review, automated testing, and secure coding practices**.**
  • Apply automation and modern tooling across the software development life cycle, including AI-enabled capabilities, to improve delivery efficiency and reliability.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS, CAPABILITIES AND SKILLS

  • Be pursuing a Bachelor’s degree or a 5th-year Master’s degree with an expected graduation between December 2027 and June 2028.
  • Pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree with expected graduation by June 2028
  • Have streams and specializations in Computer Science, Information Science, Information Technology, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Big Data, or related fields
  • Basic knowledge of industry-wide technology trends and best practices.
  • Demonstrate the ability to write secure, high-quality code in at least one programming language, following established standards and best practices.
  • Have experience collaborating with engineers, managers, and stakeholders across teams to understand problems, share ideas and feedback, and deliver reliable solutions.
  • Demonstrate strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to articulate technical concepts, document work, and collaborate effectively across teams and tools.
  • Apply automation and modern tooling to reduce manual effort and improve consistency across the software development life cycle.
  • Use approved AI development tools (for example, code drafting, refactoring, testing, and documentation) with appropriate review and validation.
  • Critically evaluate AI-generated outputs and remain accountable for final solution quality and correctness.
  • Follow responsible AI practices in engineering workflows, including secure handling of inputs and outputs and adherence to resiliency and security expectations.

Preferred Qualifications, capabilities, and skills

  • Demonstrate interpersonal and problem-solving skills, with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.
  • Bring curiosity about emerging technologies and thoughtfully assess when and how to apply them.
  • Seek opportunities to build, improve, and deliver technology that creates real-world impact.
  • Apply software engineering skills to projects involving open-ended or ambiguous problems, including breaking work into steps, experimenting with solutions, and iterating based on feedback.
  • Use AI development tools to improve efficiency with tasks such as coding, testing, debugging, or documentation.
  • Demonstrate sound judgment in validating AI-generated outputs and maintaining ownership of solution quality, correctness, and security.

FEDERAL DEPOSIT INSURANCE ACT: This position is subject to Section 19 of the Federal Deposit Insurance Act. As such, an employment offer for this position is contingent on JPMorganChase’s review of criminal conviction history, including pretrial diversions or program entries.

Locations you may join:

  • Chicago, IL
  • Columbus, OH
  • Houston, TX
  • Jersey City, NJ
  • New York Metro, NY
  • Palo Alto, CA
  • Plano, TX
  • Tampa, FL
  • Wilmington, DE

ABOUT US

You’ll benefit from a multi-billion annual investment in technology, working in one of the world’s biggest tech companies. You’ll work in an open, collaborative, and supportive culture, where our agile teams are constantly innovating, learning new skills, and at the forefront of developing new technologies and solutions.

With the scale of our business, you could impact millions of consumers, thousands of enterprise clients, and 300,000+ employees. We’re committed to advancing your career helping you acquire new skills, opportunities, and a global network of support that will help you take your career in any direction imaginable.

About You

If you’re ready to put your passion for technology to work in a way that makes a real difference, you’ll find your place in our Software Engineer Program.

To be eligible for this program, you must be authorized to work in the U.S. We do not offer any type of employment-based immigration sponsorship for this program. Likewise, JPMorgan Chase, will not provide any assistance or sign any documentation in support of any other form of immigration sponsorship or benefit including optional practical training (OPT) or curricular practical training (CPT.)

What’s Next?

To be considered for the Code for Good Hackathon, you must complete the following steps:

  1. Please ensure read the Official Rules before you start this application.
  2. Help us learn about you by submitting a complete and thoughtful application, which includes your resume. Your application and resume is a way for us to initially get to know you, so it’s important to complete all relevant application questions so we have as much information about you as possible.
  3. On your application form, please select the JPMorganChase locations that you are most interested in learning about. Selected applicants will be invited to attend one of the hackathons with technologists and recruiters best matched to your work location preference.
  4. After you submit your application, we will review it to determine whether you meet certain required qualifications.
  5. If you are advanced to the next step of the process, you’ll receive an email invitation to complete a coding challenge powered by HackerRank. Your application will not be considered for further review until you have completed this step. This is your opportunity to further bring your resume to life and showcase your experience for our recruiting team and hiring managers.
  6. Selected applicants will be notified via email with final event details.
  7. Coders will need to bring their own laptops to the event.

Code for Good Event Dates and Locations:

  • Brooklyn, NY: October 16th- October 17th
    • Welcoming participants interested in Jersey City, NJ, New York, NY, Palo Alto, CA, Chicago, IL or Wilmington, DE
    • Application Deadline: September 18th, 2026
  • Columbus, OH: November 6th- November 7th
    • Welcoming participants interested in Columbus, OH, Plano, TX, Houston, TX or Tampa, FL
    • Application Deadline: October 9th, 2026

JPMorganChase is committed to creating an inclusive work environment that respects all people for their unique skills, backgrounds, and professional experiences. We will provide reasonable accommodations for applicants with disabilities.

Visit jpmorganchase.com/careers for upcoming events, career advice, our locations and more.

Learn More HERE

About Us

JPMorganChase, one of the oldest financial institutions, offers innovative financial solutions to millions of consumers, small businesses and many of the world’s most prominent corporate, institutional and government clients under the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands. Our history spans over 200 years and today we are a leader in investment banking, consumer and small business banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management.

We offer a competitive total rewards package including base salary determined based on the role, experience, skill set and location. Those in eligible roles may receive commission-based pay and/or discretionary incentive compensation, paid in the form of cash or forfeitable equity, awarded in recognition of individual achievements and contributions. We also offer a range of benefits and programs to meet employee needs, based on eligibility. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage, on-site health and wellness centers, a retirement savings plan, backup childcare, tuition reimbursement, mental health support, financial coaching and more. Additional details about total compensation and benefits will be provided during the hiring process.

We recognize that our people are our strength and the diverse talents they bring to our global workforce are directly linked to our success. We are an equal opportunity employer and place a high value on diversity and inclusion at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of any protected attribute, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. We also make reasonable accommodations for applicants’ and employees’ religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. Visit our FAQs for more information about requesting an accommodation.

item.content:encoded:
BRIDGE X 2026 is a year-long youth exposure programme by BRAC designed to give undergraduate university students practical exposure to development work, social innovation, social business, and leadership. The programme is intended for students who want to move beyond classroom learning, engage with real-world social challenges, and develop the skills, confidence, and networks needed to contribute to meaningful change.

Through a structured journey involving practical problem-solving, professional development, campus engagement, and interaction with development practitioners, selected students, known as BRIDGE X focals, will have the opportunity to connect their academic knowledge with practical action.

The programme offers an opportunity for young people to understand how development organisations approach complex social challenges while also encouraging participants to bring their own ideas, perspectives, and initiatives to their university campuses and wider communities.

BRIDGE X 2026 at a Glance

  • Programme: BRIDGE X
  • Organiser: BRAC
  • Duration: One year
  • Target participants: Undergraduate university students
  • Academic level: Primarily students in their second or third year
  • Academic discipline: Any discipline
  • Focus areas: Social development, social impact, social innovation, leadership, professional development and youth engagement
  • Format: A combination of planned sessions, workshops, practical activities, problem-solving, and campus engagement
  • Role: BRIDGE X focal
  • Application process: Online application, take-home assessment and interview
  • Deadline: 26 August 2026
  • Application: Applicants should use the official BRIDGE X application portal provided by BRAC.

BRAC describes the initiative as an opportunity for undergraduate students to gain access to its wider ecosystem of solutions and develop a closer understanding of what it takes to become part of the next generation of leaders who can drive positive social change.

What Is the BRIDGE X Programme?

BRIDGE X is structured around the idea of creating a bridge between academic knowledge and practical action.

University education can provide students with theoretical knowledge, analytical frameworks, and technical skills. However, understanding how social problems operate in real communities and how organisations design solutions to those problems often requires practical exposure.

BRIDGE X seeks to provide that exposure.

Participants will have opportunities to explore development challenges, work on cases related to social development, engage with practitioners, and contribute to conversations about important social issues. They will also be encouraged to bring these conversations back to their campuses through awareness activities, seminars, workshops, and other initiatives.

The programme therefore combines several dimensions of youth development:

  1. Practical learning
  2. Professional development
  3. Leadership development
  4. Social impact exposure
  5. Campus engagement
  6. Networking
  7. Career exploration

Rather than being limited to conventional classroom-based learning, the programme is designed to expose students to the realities of working on complex social and development challenges.

Why BRIDGE X Is an Important Opportunity for University Students

Students interested in development, international affairs, social innovation, public policy, communications, community development, business, sustainability, and related fields can benefit from opportunities that allow them to understand how ideas are translated into action.

BRIDGE X provides such exposure by encouraging participants to examine real development problems and think about potential solutions.

The programme can help students understand:

  • How development organisations approach social challenges.
  • How social innovation can contribute to solving complex problems.
  • How social businesses operate within development ecosystems.
  • How young people can contribute to social change.
  • How to communicate important social issues within university communities.
  • How professional networks can support future career development.
  • How academic knowledge can be applied to real-world situations.
  • What early-career pathways may exist within the development sector.

For students considering careers in development organisations, international organisations, NGOs, social enterprises, research institutions, or other impact-oriented organisations, this type of exposure can provide valuable insight into the sector.

Key Benefits of BRIDGE X 2026

1. Practical Exposure to Social Development

One of the central benefits of BRIDGE X is the opportunity to gain exposure to development practice.

Participants will work with cases and challenges grounded in real social development issues. This can help them move from simply studying social problems to thinking critically about how solutions can be designed and implemented.

The experience can strengthen practical skills such as the following:

  • Problem-solving
  • Critical thinking
  • Research
  • Idea development
  • Communication
  • Collaboration
  • Leadership
  • Presentation
  • Social impact analysis

2. Opportunity to Explore Social Impact

BRIDGE X gives students an opportunity to explore the broader world of social impact.

Participants can gain exposure to areas including development practice, social innovation, and social business, helping them understand how organisations attempt to create sustainable solutions to social challenges.

This is particularly relevant for students who want careers where professional work is connected to social and community outcomes.

3. Networking and Professional Connections

Networking is another important element of the programme.

Selected participants will have opportunities to connect with:

  • Fellow university students
  • Development practitioners
  • BRAC professionals
  • Other young people interested in social change
  • Potential professional contacts
  • Learning and conference opportunities

Building relationships at university can be particularly valuable because many future opportunities are developed through professional networks, peer communities, and exposure to practitioners.

4. Professional and Career Preparation

BRIDGE X is also intended to help participants prepare for their future careers.

Students can gain insight into workplace expectations and early-career pathways while developing experience that may strengthen their future applications.

The programme may be particularly useful for students who are still exploring what type of career they want to pursue after university.

Participants can use the experience to better understand:

  • Their professional interests
  • Their strengths and capabilities
  • The development sector
  • Social-impact careers
  • Leadership opportunities
  • Potential internship pathways
  • Early-career opportunities

5. Potential Future Career Opportunities

Participation in BRIDGE X does not automatically guarantee an internship or employment opportunity with BRAC.

However, the programme is designed to provide experience and visibility that may be useful when participants later pursue internships or early-career opportunities.

Students interested in BRAC’s work can therefore use the programme as an opportunity to better understand the organisation and the types of professional environments within the development sector.

The BRIDGE X Selection Process

BRAC has outlined a three-stage selection process for BRIDGE X.

The first stage is the online application.

Applicants will be asked to provide information about their:

  • Experiences
  • Motivation
  • Engagement with social issues
  • Interest in making change happen

A strong application should clearly demonstrate why the applicant is interested in BRIDGE X and provide concrete examples of initiative, community involvement, leadership or social-impact activities.

Stage 2: Take-Home Assessment

Applicants who progress through the initial stage will complete a take-home assessment designed specifically for the programme.

This stage is likely to provide applicants with an opportunity to demonstrate their thinking and problem-solving abilities.

Applicants should approach the assessment carefully and demonstrate the following:

  • Logical reasoning
  • Creativity
  • Understanding of the issue presented
  • Practical thinking
  • Clear communication
  • Evidence-based reasoning where appropriate
  • Feasible solutions

Stage 3: Interview

Shortlisted candidates will proceed to an interview.

  4. Examples of leadership or initiative.
  5. How they have contributed to solving a problem.
  6. What they hope to learn from the programme.
  7. How they would engage their university campus.
  8. How they would balance BRIDGE X responsibilities with their studies.
